title: Graph Beta: mint the server-owned launch-template producers
description:
HALF B of the governor's SPLIT decision on task-a3e8a02ddb864c689ac66de7b66bfceb (comment-cf245bba, 2026-08-18 08:42Z, standing authority). Filed by architect-c9e91335 while re-planning Half A. Half A (task-a3e8a02d) is the input-manifest half and is now planned; THIS task is the launch-template half and is a PREREQUISITE of the same consumer.

DO NOT RE-DERIVE the measurement below — it is worker-a83aecdf's, preserved by the governor and re-confirmed at HEAD f96995d8.

THE ROOT PROBLEM, and it is a design gap rather than a lookup: `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_TEMPLATE_KEYS` (apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts) declares seven fields — argv, bootstrapCredentialDigest, cwd, environment, launchSelection, limits, runtime. Three of them have NO server-owned producer anywhere in the repo:

1. **argv** — `NodeMission` is `{instructions, test, title, workspace}` (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:47-52) and carries no argv. `providerCapabilities` / `ProviderCapabilities` has ZERO matches repo-wide. Nothing composes an argument vector from server facts.

2. **launchSelection** — the only production surface is `snapshotLaunchSelection(value: unknown)` at packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-launch-selection.ts:167, which is a VALIDATOR OVER CALLER INPUT, not a selector. Zero matches for selectClaudeLaunch / chooseLaunch / resolveLaunch. Daemon production carries only the pass-through `template["launchSelection"]` (foundation-attempt-codec.ts:125, contracts:215).

3. **limits** — daemon production has only the `template["limits"]` pass-through. The scheduler budget seam is explicitly "Caller-supplied conserved-budget admission reservation" over "a caller-supplied account view" (packages/scheduler/src/index.ts:20-24), and `projectBudgetFact` is DELIBERATELY WITHHELD because "budget-policy projection is a different seam" (:107-111).

THE TRAP THAT MAKES THIS DANGEROUS, quoted from the worker's own handoff: "A bounded SHAPE is trivially constructible — which is exactly what makes this dangerous. Declaring a type does not create a source. Anyone who closes finding (a) and then fills the bounded type from the request has shipped a caller echo wearing a server-derived label, and the suite will be green." A `validate*()` over a request field is NOT a reader; the governor's directive says so in terms.

DELIVERABLE: mint the three server-owned producers, or — where a field is legitimately caller-proposed — record that decision explicitly with an exact authenticated payload allow-list and bound, per the parent task's DoD 1. The provider-capability source is the ROOT gap: it feeds BOTH argv and launchSelection, so decide its owner and shape first. The limits producer needs a durable launch-limits projection whose seam the scheduler deliberately does not provide.

NOT IN SCOPE: the input manifest (task-a3e8a02d owns it), attempt command registration, claim/activation, provider dispatch internals, widening effect.activate, or editing the authoritative design.

CONSUMER: task-a9fd91c373c244c78df97945965a8038 (Foundation attempt ingress composition), the same consumer Half A names. Dependents citing the parent as a gating dep: task-203a5ca7 and task-933605a5.
definitionOfDone: Planning notes record the per-field authority decision for argv, launchSelection and limits — server-derived/durable versus caller-proposed-but-bounded — with the reason for each; an unresolved field blocks rather than defaults, and any caller-proposed field carries an exact authenticated payload allow-list and bound.

A server-owned provider-capability source exists and is the authority feeding BOTH argv and launchSelection; `grep -rn 'providerCapabilities\|ProviderCapabilities' --include=*.ts apps packages | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns a production producer where it returned zero repo-wide.

Each produced field is derived from durable or observed server facts, never from the dispatch request: a test supplies a caller-proposed argv, launchSelection and limits that CONTRADICT the server-derived values and asserts the server value is what lands, pinning the exact code and layer of whichever layer refused the caller's.

A mutation that fills any of the three fields from the request instead of the server source turns a NAMED test red — this is the caller-echo-wearing-a-server-label defect the split was made to prevent, and it is invisible to a green suite.
Repeated production of the same durable identity is byte-stable, and an unverifiable capability, selection or limit fails closed with an exact stable code and layer rather than defaulting.

Focused tests use real durable/host seams with nonzero generated hostile-case counts and one accepted control; daemon typecheck and test run with exit codes captured separately and nonzero Test Files/Tests count lines.
taskRails: A validate*() over a request field is NOT a reader. Declaring a bounded type does not create a source — a bounded shape filled from the request is a caller echo wearing a server-derived label, and it passes a green suite.
Decide the provider-capability source FIRST: it is the root gap feeding both argv and launchSelection, and nothing by that name exists repo-wide, so it is a design decision rather than a lookup.
Do not reimplement launch selection or workspace sealing; reuse public @moe/runner roots. `snapshotLaunchSelection` is a validator and may not be presented as the selector.
Keep this seam separate from Foundation ingress, graph projection, activation and launch execution. Do not widen effect.activate.

Fail closed with stable reason codes and layers, use TDD, target <=250 physical lines per production source, and commit only explicit owned paths by pathspec — this epic's rail 3 forbids a bare git commit because the index is shared.

implementationPlan.description:
VERIFY-OR-BLOCK GATE, and it carries a CORRECTION to this task's own description — which I wrote while planning Half A, so re-measure rather than trusting it.
(a) THE LIMITS PREMISE IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BE PLANNED AGAINST. The description (inheriting worker-a83aecdf's note) implies `limits` needs a durable launch-limits projection tied to the scheduler budget seam. Measured: `ClaudeLaunchLimits` is `{stdoutBytes, stderrBytes, tailBytes, timeoutMs}` (claude-launcher-contract.ts:75-80) — CAPTURE ceilings, not conserved budget. `claude-launcher-input.ts:172-173` already hard-bounds them at 1_048_576 / 1_048_576 / 65_536 / 600_000 and requires every value to be a positive safe integer. So the scheduler's withheld `projectBudgetFact` is IRRELEVANT here; do not build a budget projection.
(b) ARGV IS NOT FREE-FORM, which changes what "producing" it means. `verifyLaunchSelection(request.launchSelection, request.argv, request.environment)` runs INSIDE the launcher (claude-launcher.ts:190) and checks argv/env actually carry the selection in exact spellings: `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_FLAGS = {model: "--model", effort: "--effort"}` (claude-launch-selection.ts:51-52) and `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_ENV = {model: "ANTHROPIC_MODEL", effort: "CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL"}` (:65-66), with `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_RESUME_FLAGS` (:85-87) refused because a resumed session keeps the transcript's model whatever `--model` says. So argv is DERIVABLE from the selection plus the mission, and the launcher already enforces agreement.
(c) `ClaudeLaunchSelection` (claude-launch-selection.ts:93-104) is ten fields: provider, selectedModelId, modelSnapshotKind, modelSnapshotEvidence, reasoningEffort, profileRevisionId, configurationDigest, policyDigest, orchestrationDigest, concurrencyCeiling. Every one is a policy/profile/observation fact — none is a caller preference.
(d) A DURABLE PROVIDER FACT ALREADY EXISTS, which the original measurement missed: `provider.probe` is a registered bootstrap command (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:39, payload keys `["observation"]` at :108) whose handler `recordProbe` (bootstrap-services.ts:117-136) commits a `ProviderProbed` event carrying `{providerMinimumProfileRef, truthClass}`. `ProjectActivationWitness` (packages/core/src/project/project-contract.ts:25-35) carries `policyRevisionHash` and `providerMinimumProfileRef` too.
(e) THE REAL REMAINING GAP: nothing defines the CONTENT behind `providerMinimumProfileRef`, and there is no reader for `ProviderProbed`. `grep -rn 'providerCapabilities\|ProviderCapabilities' --include=*.ts apps packages | grep -v '\.test\.'` must still return ZERO.
Record every command and result; the corrections above belong in planningNotes and in the completion notes.

implementationPlan.description:
RECORD THE PER-FIELD AUTHORITY MATRIX — DoD 1, and it is the deliverable that makes the other steps legible. Write it into the header of the producer module, not only a completion note.
Decide and justify all three rows, plus the four already-settled ones for context:
- **launchSelection** — SERVER-DERIVED. Its ten fields split into three sources, all server-owned: `provider` is a literal; `selectedModelId`/`modelSnapshotKind`/`modelSnapshotEvidence` come from OBSERVING the installed runtime (`observeInstalledClaudeRuntime`, reachable through the bare root via nested `export *` — do not grep index.ts for it, that is a false negative); `reasoningEffort`, `profileRevisionId`, `configurationDigest`, `policyDigest`, `orchestrationDigest` and `concurrencyCeiling` come from DURABLE project/policy state. No caller field participates.
- **argv** — SERVER-DERIVED, composed from the selection plus the node mission. It MUST name the model and effort in the exact spellings `verifyLaunchSelection` demands and MUST carry no member of `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_RESUME_FLAGS`. State plainly that the launcher's gate is a CHECK, not the producer: passing its check does not make a caller-supplied argv server-derived.
- **limits** — SERVER-OWNED, pinned by the durable policy revision, and bounded independently by the launcher's own ceilings. Record the corrected reading from step 1(a): these are capture ceilings, not budget, so no budget seam is involved.
Also record why the caller CANNOT propose any of the three: each one, if caller-supplied, lets an agent choose its own model, its own effort, its own capture ceiling — i.e. grade its own homework. Any field you cannot source from a server fact BLOCKS rather than defaults; if the durable policy state turns out not to carry a digest this selection needs, stop and report blocked with the missing field named, rather than inventing a placeholder digest.

`produceLaunchTemplateFields({capabilities, runtimeObservation, mission, policy})` returning the three fields plus an exact refusal:
- **launchSelection**: assemble the ten fields from the capability read and the runtime observation. `provider` is the server literal `"claude"`. Model id, snapshot kind and snapshot evidence come from the OBSERVED runtime. Effort, the four digests, the profile revision and the concurrency ceiling come from durable policy. implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN DIFF, AND IT IS FIXED. Reading the producer as an attacker rather than as its author: every guard reflected on an unknown record (`hasExactKeys` -> `Object.keys`, then property reads) with no containment. A REVOKED PROXY makes `Object.keys` itself throw, and a getter can throw on any read, so a hostile capabilities object made the producer CRASH rather than refuse — and a crash is not a refusal, it tells the caller nothing and unwinds through whatever composed it. The runner's own validators contain exactly this (`isHostileObject` before any reflection) and the landed resolver wraps its durable read in try/catch; mine did neither.
FIX: the exported function is now a total wrapper — `try { return compose(input) } catch { return refuse("LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_INPUT_HOSTILE", ...) }` — with a new closed code, and the caught error's message is deliberately NOT echoed (it would carry the caller's own text back out of a failure path). Two new tests cover it: a revoked proxy and a throwing getter, each asserting `not.toThrow()` BEFORE asserting the code. Drill 6 (below) proves the guard is load-bearing.

THE FIX FORCED A FILE SPLIT, with the measured evidence the plan asked for: the wrapper pushed launch-template-producer.ts to 259 lines, over the 250 rail. The vocabulary and capability admission moved to a sibling, apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-authority.ts, with its own exact one-line LF bridge. `wc -l` at HEAD: producer 174, authority 137. The producer re-exports the vocabulary so consumers still have one import path.

THE REST OF THE CHECKLIST, walked rather than skimmed:
- CALLER REACH: the signature names no dispatch request, no optional override, no default. The input record is exact (an extra key refuses and is NAMED), and — a hole I closed with a test rather than an argument — a capabilities record carrying a planted `argv` contributes nothing, because the selection is built field by NAME and never spread. Test: "ignores an argv planted ON the capability record instead of copying it".
- DEFAULTED FIELDS: none. All six selection text fields, the concurrency ceiling and the capability schema digest each refuse when absent; the four limits are decided by the public validator; every argv element is checked. UNKNOWN model evidence and UNKNOWN effort refuse rather than being carried.
- ARGV/ENVIRONMENT AGREEMENT: both halves are built from the same two values, asserted in three tests, and drill 5 kills any disagreement — including at the real launcher gate.
- truthClass: NOT carried by this module, and that is the landed design rather than a collapse. `ProviderCapabilities` exposes no truthClass; the resolver enforces STRONG_TRUTH = DAEMON_VERIFIED|HUMAN_APPROVED and REFUSES weak truth upstream (tested here through a real AGENT_REPORTED probe -> PROVIDER_PROFILE_TRUTH_UNVERIFIED). Nothing in my diff can promote a claim to a fact because no weak claim reaches it.
- RESTAMPING: none. LAUNCH_LIMITS and PROVIDER_PROFILE_READER codes travel as `upstream` untranslated; my layer is module-private and published as a closed type, so the security roster gains no unregistered boundary.
- CONCURRENCY: the producer is pure over its arguments — no store handle, no file, no cache, no subprocess, nothing to close on an error path and nothing to double-write on a retry. Two concurrent calls with the same durable identity return byte-identical frozen records.
- REMAINING THEORETICAL RISK, disclosed rather than hidden: an in-process caller that forged a whole DAEMON_VERIFIED/DURABLE/CURRENT record with valid bounded fields would be admitted. That is not reachable from a dispatch request and no in-process fence can close it; the durable authority is the resolver's, and this module refuses everything short of that shape.
- FOLLOW-UP, out of this task's scope by its own NOT-IN-SCOPE clause: the producer is not yet published from the daemon root and not yet wired into any dispatch path; foundation-dispatch-derivation.ts:32 still records launchTemplate as caller-proposed. Wiring belongs to the consumer seam.

A caller who supplies both argv and selection passes the gate while having chosen its own model — grading its own homework.

Policy can say which model is permitted; only observation can say which one is installed.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD d543f71e. Two claims in this task's own description (which I authored during Half A planning) are WRONG and are corrected here.

CORRECTION 1 — LIMITS ARE NOT BUDGET. `ClaudeLaunchLimits` = `{stdoutBytes, stderrBytes, tailBytes, timeoutMs}` (claude-launcher-contract.ts:75-80). `claude-launcher-input.ts:170-175` requires every value to be a positive safe integer and caps them at 1_048_576 / 1_048_576 / 65_536 / 600_000. These are capture and timeout ceilings. The scheduler's "caller-supplied conserved-budget admission" seam and its withheld `projectBudgetFact` have nothing to do with them.

CORRECTION 2 — A DURABLE PROVIDER FACT ALREADY EXISTS. `provider.probe` is registered (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:39, payload `["observation"]` at :108), sequenced after `project.register` (bootstrap-sequence.ts:34), and its handler `recordProbe` (bootstrap-services.ts:117-136) validates `providerMinimumProfileRef` and `truthClass` against `RUNTIME_LIFECYCLES.TRUTH_CLASS` and commits a `ProviderProbed` event. `ProjectActivationWitness` (packages/core/src/project/project-contract.ts:25-35) carries `policyRevisionHash` and `providerMinimumProfileRef`. So the durable seam is real; what is missing is a READER and the profile's CONTENT.

STILL ZERO, as the split recorded: `grep -rn 'providerCapabilities|ProviderCapabilities' --include=*.ts apps packages | grep -v '.test.'` returns nothing. That symbol is what DoD 2 asks this task to create.

WHAT A SELECTION IS: `ClaudeLaunchSelection` (claude-launch-selection.ts:93-104) has ten fields — provider, selectedModelId, modelSnapshotKind, modelSnapshotEvidence, reasoningEffort, profileRevisionId, configurationDigest, policyDigest, orchestrationDigest, concurrencyCeiling. Six are policy/profile digests or ceilings; three are model EVIDENCE; one is a literal. None is a user preference, which is why caller-proposed is not a defensible reading for this field.

ARGV IS CONSTRAINED, NOT FREE. `claude-launcher.ts:190` calls `verifyLaunchSelection(request.launchSelection, request.argv, request.environment)`. The vocabulary is frozen and measured from the installed binary: `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_FLAGS = {model: "--model", effort: "--effort"}` (:51-52) and `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_ENV = {model: "ANTHROPIC_MODEL", effort: "CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL"}` (:65-66). The env comment is load-bearing: the environment value OVERRIDES the flag, so argv and environment must agree or the certified model is not the one that ran. `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_RESUME_FLAGS` (:85-87) are refused because a resumed session keeps the transcript's model whatever `--model` says — "argv alone cannot tell its two meanings apart, and an unprovable model stays unproven".

EVIDENCE MAY BE ABSENT BY DESIGN: `CLAUDE_MODEL_EVIDENCE_ABSENT = "UNKNOWN"` (:88). The producer must decide deliberately what to do when the observed runtime yields UNKNOWN evidence, and record it.

NESTED-EXPORT TRAP, carried forward from Half A: `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` (claude-host-runtime.ts:201) and `createClaudeRuntimePinRequest` reach the @moe/runner bare root through nested `export *` (index.ts -> surface/claude-surface.js -> claude-discovery-surface.js). Grepping index.ts for them is a FALSE NEGATIVE.

MISSION SHAPE: `NodeMission` = `{instructions, test, title, workspace}` (agent-wrapper.ts:47-52) — confirmed to carry no argv, as the split recorded.

DEPENDENCY EDGE: apps/daemon declares @moe/runner and @moe/scheduler with matching pnpm-lock importer links; Half A's compiled bare-specifier probe passed clean. Re-probe in step 1 only.
planningNotes.risks:
1) THE CALLER ECHO IS THE FAILURE THIS TASK EXISTS TO PREVENT, and it passes a green suite. A bounded type filled from the request satisfies every shape assertion. The defences are the three-way contradiction test (caller values that DISAGREE, server values must win) and drill #1 run three times — once per field. One combined drill would pass if only one field were genuinely server-sourced, which is precisely the half-finished state to avoid.

2) `verifyLaunchSelection` IS A CHECK, NOT A PRODUCER. Passing it proves argv agrees with a selection; it says nothing about who chose the selection. Do not let a reviewer or a future reader treat the gate as evidence of server derivation.

3) ARGV AND ENVIRONMENT MUST AGREE. The env override WINS over the flag per the runner's own comment, so emitting model X in argv and model Y in the environment certifies a model that never ran. Assert agreement explicitly.

4) A DEFAULTED CAPABILITY IS FAIL-OPEN. An empty capability set reads as "no restrictions". Absent probe must refuse, and drill #2 proves it.

5) TRUTH CLASS IS A SILENT AUTHORITY LEAK IF COLLAPSED. `recordProbe` stores it deliberately; a reader that drops it promotes AGENT_REPORTED to DAEMON_VERIFIED with no visible symptom.

6) A STABILITY TEST OVER A CONSTANT IS VACUOUS. Pair the byte-stability assertion with one proving a changed policy revision CHANGES the output, or a producer that ignores its inputs passes both.

7) UNKNOWN MODEL EVIDENCE is a designed state, not an error to paper over. Decide refuse-versus-carry, record it, and test the chosen arm.

8) FOREIGN RED IN THIS PACKAGE was recorded by Half A (goal-services.test.ts, agent-wrapper.ts, other agents' uncommitted work). Capture the baseline before editing; the owned-path delta must be empty; do not repair them and do not let them mask your own red.

9) FOUR VOCABULARIES CAN REFUSE: this producer, the capability reader, the runner's selection gate, and the launcher. Pin code AND layer on every arm or a swallowed code goes unnoticed.

10) THE CHAIN IS NOT CLEARED BY THIS TASK ALONE. Half A must also land before task-a9fd91c3 can compose; task-203a5ca7 and task-933605a5 cite the parent as gating.
